en.title: General insurers must seek MER advice from "its Approved Actuary"; it is unclear whether insurers not otherwise required to have one must appoint one (PINS and TRR)
en.summary: PINS Schedule 5, paragraph 10 applies to General Insurance Business. Paragraph 10.2(2) requires an insurer to "seek advice from its Approved Actuary" about its maximum event retention if it issues policies without a maximum amount insured, insures risks in multiple lines of business or has a complex portfolio. Under PINS 2.2.2(2) an Approved Actuary is mandatory for a general insurer only in certain cases, and PINS 9.2 deals with insurers "not required to have an Approved Actuary". The text does not say whether paragraph 10.2(2) itself requires such an insurer to appoint one, or whether it may use the independent actuary described in PINS 9.2.3. TRR Schedule 5, paragraph 10.2(2) is the same.
en.correction: Please clarify whether an insurer subject to Schedule 5 paragraph 10.2(2), but outside rule 2.2.2(2), must appoint an Approved Actuary or may use the actuary described in rule 9.2.3 (and the same for TRR).
